standard_prerequisites.name: Isotypic decomposition and polynomial-degree characterization on S_n
standard_prerequisites.statement: Real functions on S_n decompose orthogonally into V^lambda. Their coordinate polynomial degree is the largest n-lambda_1 among nonzero components.
standard_prerequisites.use: Locate a highest-degree nonzero component of the restriction and infer the degree lower bound from the lifted component. Independent review must accept this as a stated standard representation-theoretic input, not an unproved new local lemma.

standard_prerequisites.name: Young column-antisymmetrizer spanning theorem
standard_prerequisites.statement: V^lambda is spanned by chi_(s,t)=sum over pi in C(t) of sign(pi)*e_(s,t^pi), with the tableaux and e-functions defined in the source.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: source331-364; Sagan, The Symmetric Group, Chapter2.
standard_prerequisites.use: Choose a witness with nonzero inner product and lift it by adding a singleton row. The lift/cancellation argument is the counted proof obligation.

core_obligations: Lift a highest-degree nonzero Young antisymmetrizer witness by appending the distinguished element in a singleton row.
Use support on the fixed-point coset to annihilate column permutations moving that element, and identify the remaining signed inner product with its S_(n-1) witness.

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to the n-to-n coset and extract a nonzero tableau witness for the restriction.
Append a singleton row and compute the new first-row deficit.
Use support to annihilate moving-column terms, identify the surviving inner product exactly and obtain the degree lower bound.

difficulty_reason: The spectral degree and Young spanning theorems are explicit standard representation inputs, but the singleton-row witness and support cancellation supply a genuine nonroutine strict degree reduction.

compared.difference: The public primary is uniqueness of maximum2-intersecting perfect-matchings families. This is a degree-drop statement for arbitrary Boolean functions on permutations supported on a1-coset.

review_checkpoints: Appending a singleton row gives a legitimate partition mu of n with mu_1=lambda_1, so its degree deficit increases by1.
A column permutation moving n cannot contribute on a permutation fixing n because the new singleton row in s forces n into the corresponding singleton row in t-prime.
When the column permutation fixes n, signs and row-incidence functions restrict exactly to those for S_(n-1); no injectivity of a restriction map is assumed.
The source treats n=1 and the zero restriction separately.
